findings.title: Incompatible duplicate domain models between W1 and W2 in ucc-core
findings.expected: Single authoritative domain model in crates/ucc-core shared across workspace
findings.actual: W1 and W2 defined conflicting structs (UccProfile vs Profile, ProfileCpu vs CpuSettings, etc.)
findings.consequence: Compilation failure and unresolvable merge conflict upon branch integration
findings.suggested_direction: Adopt W1 domain models in ucc-core, remove W2 models.rs, and adapt ucc-config to use W1 types
findings.resolution: W2 removed duplicate models.rs, merged rust/migration, and ucc-config now cleanly uses ucc-core domain models

findings.title: Profile ID and count divergence in defaults.rs (M2.4 violation)
findings.trigger: Loading existing /etc/ucc/settings or querying D-Bus GetDefaultProfilesJSON
findings.expected: 4 canonical built-in profile IDs preserved exactly: 'Max Energy Save [Built-in]', 'Quiet [Built-in]', 'Office [Built-in]', 'High Performance [Built-in]'
findings.actual: W2 created 3 profiles with custom IDs: 'quiet', 'balanced', 'performance', dropping Max Energy Save
findings.consequence: Existing settings referencing canonical IDs fail to map, D-Bus clients break
findings.suggested_direction: Restore all 4 canonical profile IDs in defaults.rs matching C++ DefaultProfileIDs
findings.resolution: Restored all 4 canonical profile IDs in defaults.rs, alias resolution added for backward compatibility

findings.title: Wire JSON key casing mismatch on uppercase acronyms
findings.trigger: Serializing/deserializing profile fan curves with naive camelCase
findings.expected: Wire JSON keys retain exact casing: tableCPU, tableGPU, autoControlWC
findings.actual: Default camelCase serializes as tableCpu, tableGpu, autoControlWc
findings.consequence: Silent data drop of fan curve tables when communicating with legacy GUI/daemon
findings.resolution: Added explicit serde rename attributes for tableCPU, tableGPU, autoControlWC, odmPowerLimits, nvidiaCTGPOffset

findings.title: Pump table step index vs discrete PumpVoltage wire code confusion
findings.trigger: Passing pump curve speed value directly as voltage code
findings.expected: Table speed (0..4) translated via pumpSpeedToVoltage mapping (0=Off, 1=V7, 2=V8, 3=V11, 4=V12)
findings.actual: Raw index 1 represents 12V which is strictly forbidden on LCT coolers in production
findings.consequence: Hardware safety violation if curve index is sent directly to ioctl/UART
findings.suggested_direction: Use W1 pump_speed_to_voltage translation function consistently across config and hardware
findings.resolution: Implemented bidirectional pump_speed_to_voltage and voltage_to_pump_speed translators in ucc-core::fan

findings.title: NvmlWrapper permanently locks device_count to 0 if instantiated while discrete GPU is in runtime D3cold sleep
findings.trigger: Starting daemon/NvmlWrapper on battery or hybrid graphics system where NVIDIA dGPU is runtime suspended ('suspended' in power/runtime_status), then later waking the GPU and calling get_telemetry(0) or get_power_limit_constraints(0)
findings.expected: When dGPU transitions from suspended to active, ensure_active_and_initialized() initializes NVML, discovers available devices, updates device_count dynamically, and allows telemetry queries
findings.actual: device_count is an immutable u32 initialized to 0 in new(). In get_telemetry/get_power_limit_constraints, the check 'if index >= self.device_count' executes BEFORE ensure_active_and_initialized(), immediately returning Err(NvmlError::NoGpuFound). Even inside ensure_active_and_initialized(), the result of fn_device_get_count is discarded without updating self.device_count
findings.consequence: Discrete GPU telemetry, temperature monitoring, utilization, and power limit controls remain permanently broken (returning NoGpuFound) for the entire lifetime of the process whenever the daemon boots while dGPU is suspended
findings.reproducer: Instantiate NvmlWrapper with mock power_guard returning is_dgpu_awake() == false. Subsequently set power_guard to return true and invoke get_telemetry(0). The call returns Err(NvmlError::NoGpuFound) instead of telemetry.
findings.suggested_direction: 1. Change device_count in NvmlWrapper to Arc<AtomicU32> (or AtomicU32). 2. In ensure_active_and_initialized(), after successful fn_init(), query device count and store with self.device_count.store(count, Ordering::SeqCst). 3. Call ensure_active_and_initialized() prior to index >= self.device_count.load() check in get_telemetry, get_power_limit_constraints, and set_power_limit.

findings.title: TuxedoIoDevice::read_clevo_interface_string allocates 20-byte buffer instead of 50 bytes required by Clevo kernel driver ABI
findings.trigger: Invoking read_clevo_interface_string() on Clevo hardware platform
findings.expected: Kernel ABI buffer length for R_CL_HW_IF_STR is 50 bytes, matching C++ baseline in clevo.h:45 (m_io.ioctlCall(R_CL_HW_IF_STR, interfaceIdStr, 50))
findings.actual: read_clevo_interface_string() passes Self::VERSION_BUFFER_LEN (20 bytes) to read_str
findings.consequence: Potential kernel-to-userspace heap buffer overflow via copy_to_user if Clevo driver writes more than 20 bytes, or truncation of interface string causing hardware identification failure
findings.reproducer: Simulate R_CL_HW_IF_STR returning a 30-byte identification string; verify 20-byte buffer causes out-of-bounds write or truncation
findings.suggested_direction: Define CLEVO_IF_STR_BUFFER_LEN: usize = 50 and use it in read_clevo_interface_string()

findings.title: Clevo W_CL_FANAUTO ioctl requires 0x0f bitmask argument but lacks dedicated safe method
findings.trigger: Calling call_none(requests::W_CL_FANAUTO) expecting fan auto behavior similar to Uniwill W_UW_FANAUTO
findings.expected: Clevo fan auto requires passing integer bitmask 0x0f (_IOW(MAGIC_WRITE_CL, 0x11, int32_t*)), whereas Uniwill uses _IO(MAGIC_WRITE_UW, 0x14) with no argument
findings.actual: W_CL_FANAUTO is exposed as a raw request code without a dedicated high-level method, creating a hazard where a developer calling call_none passes no argument and causes the kernel driver to dereference invalid memory
findings.consequence: Kernel driver dereferences invalid pointer in ioctl handler on Clevo hardware, failing fan auto operation
findings.reproducer: Audit request macro: _iow_ptr encodes IOC_WRITE with size 8, requiring pointer to int32_t
findings.suggested_direction: Add set_fans_auto_clevo(&self) -> Result<(), IoctlError> sending 0x0f via write_i32, and set_fans_auto_uniwill(&self) -> Result<(), IoctlError> invoking call_none(W_UW_FANAUTO)

findings.title: NvidiaPowerGuard::find_nvidia_devices fails open if PCI class node is unreadable
findings.trigger: A sysfs PCI device entry with NVIDIA vendor (0x10de) where class attribute is temporarily unreadable or missing
findings.expected: Fail closed: device should only be classified as a graphics controller if class attribute exists and starts with 0x03 (display controller), matching GpuSysfs.hpp:48
findings.actual: if class_path.exists() condition skips filtering if class_path is absent or fails to read, adding the device unconditionally
findings.consequence: Non-graphics NVIDIA devices (audio controllers 0x0403xx, USB-C controllers) could be misidentified as dGPU graphics devices and prevent sleep
findings.reproducer: Create mock sysfs device with vendor 0x10de without class file; find_nvidia_devices returns it as an active GPU
findings.suggested_direction: Ensure device is only included if class is successfully read and starts with '0x03' or '03'
